library.name: The Sick and Suffering
library.description: For those facing illness, surgery, chronic pain, or difficult diagnoses

prayers.name: Option A — Healer of bodies
prayers.text: Healer of bodies and souls, we bring before you this morning those wrestling with illness and pain. We name [names] who carry burdens too heavy to bear alone. We remember that Jesus himself knew suffering—not as punishment, but as the place where God's mercy can reach us most deeply. Grant them not false comfort, but your real presence; not escape from their condition, but the resurrection-hope that even now, in the middle of this, you are making something new. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God who draws near
prayers.text: God who draws near to the suffering, we lift up those facing surgery this week and those whose diagnoses have filled them with fear. Their bodies feel like enemies; they are learning the humbling truth that we are not gods of our own health. In their vulnerability, may they find something harder than strength—may they find you. May the hands of surgeons be sure, the results be clear, and the recovery be gentle. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — Tender witness
prayers.text: Tender witness to all our frailty, turn your attention to those living with chronic pain, who wake each day to a familiar enemy that will not leave. Their courage goes mostly unseen and unsung. Give them the grace to grieve what they have lost without losing hope in what remains. Remind them that endurance is not a virtue they must manufacture—it is a gift you give, moment by moment. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — Foundation of all mercy
prayers.text: Foundation of all mercy, we come to you on behalf of those whose suffering has become their entire horizon. In their despair, they wonder if healing is even possible, or if they are simply abandoned. We do not pretend to have answers to their deepest questions. But we know that on a cross, you suffered with the suffering. Meet them there—not with explanations, but with presence. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — Lord of all seasons
prayers.text: Lord of all seasons, we remember those whose illness has interrupted life—the athlete who cannot run, the worker who cannot work, the parent who cannot care as they once did. Their loss is real and should be grieved. Grant them the strange gift of finding meaning not in what they can achieve, but in what they have been given to receive. May they discover, in their weakness, the sufficiency of your grace. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option F — Father of compassion
prayers.text: Father of compassion, we bring the mothers and fathers sitting in waiting rooms, the children trying to understand why their parent looks different now, the spouses learning to live with sickness instead of health. We ask not that you remove this cup—we ask that you fill it with your presence. Give wisdom to the doctors. Give courage to the patients. Give peace to those who wait. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option G — Word made flesh
prayers.text: Word made flesh who suffered hunger and pain, we remember that sickness is not spiritual failure but the common inheritance of mortal bodies. We name those struggling under the weight of guilt—believing their diagnosis is somehow their fault. Absolve them of this burden. Teach them that they are loved not because they are healthy, but because they are yours. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option H — God whose love outlasts all
prayers.text: God whose love outlasts all suffering, we bring those whose sickness has stretched beyond our ability to understand—those whose symptoms have no name, whose doctors have reached the limits of what they can do. In this awful uncertainty, we anchor ourselves in you. You are not confused by their condition. You are not surprised by their pain. You are not too far away to reach them. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: The Grieving and Bereaved
library.description: For those mourning death, loss, or deep sorrow

prayers.name: Option A — God who grieves
prayers.text: God who grieves, we come to you with the raw truth that someone has died, and the world has become a different world. We name [name] who has passed, and we name those left behind whose hearts are torn. Jesus wept at the tomb of his friend. You do not ask us to leap from sorrow to resurrection hope in a single breath. Meet us in the grave where we are—and then, slowly, raise us up. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — Eternal Word
prayers.text: Eternal Word, we remember that grief is the price we pay for love. [Names] had someone they loved, and now that person is gone. The empty chair. The unanswered phone call. The holidays that will be different. We do not ask you to make this okay. We ask that you be present in it, that the one who died is held safely in your eternal care, and that the living might, someday, find joy again. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — Resurrection Lord
prayers.text: Resurrection Lord, we come to you with the weight of unexpected loss—a death that came too soon, that was not prepared for, that has shattered our sense of order. We do not understand why. We may not understand for a long time. But we trust that [name] has passed from this life into your hands, and that is enough. Carry the grieving through this long darkness. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — Keeper of our beloved
prayers.text: Keeper of our beloved dead, we bring to you this morning those who are grieving the loss of a spouse, a parent, a child, a friend. The loss is specific and personal—not abstract. We do not come to you with faith that overcomes this sorrow, but with a sorrow that is drawn toward you. Hold them. Remind them that love is stronger than death, and that the dead are not lost to you. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — God of all comfort
prayers.text: God of all comfort, we remember that grief is not a problem to solve but a reality to walk through. We name those who are in the early days of loss, still numb; those in the middle days, when the waves crash without warning; and those in the long days, learning to live with absence. Do not let them grieve alone. Bind them to a community of mourners who know that you are good even in this. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option F — Ancient of Days
prayers.text: Ancient of Days, you have seen all generations—those who die are not lost in your eyes, but gathered into your eternal communion. We remember those who die without faith, without closure, without goodbyes. We entrust them to your mercy, which is larger than our understanding. For those left behind in confusion or guilt, bring a slow peace. Let them discover that you do not lose those whom you love. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option G — Christ our hope
prayers.text: Christ our hope, we come to you with grief that has been compounded—loss piling upon loss, until some feel that they can bear no more. One person has died, and the weight of it has cracked open older griefs. We ask not for burden-free lives, but for strength to carry these burdens toward you. Meet us in our sadness and remake it into something holy. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option H — Father of mercies
prayers.text: Father of mercies, we remember those grieving loss that no one else understands—a friendship broken, a dream deferred, a version of life that will never be. Not all grief is about death, yet it is grief nonetheless. We name these hidden losses and ask that you see them. Validate the sorrow of those who mourn what they were hoping for. Teach them that loss can be a strange teacher. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: Mental Health and Emotional Suffering
library.description: For those facing depression, anxiety, trauma, crisis, or despair

prayers.name: Option A — Light in darkness
prayers.text: Light in darkness, we bring to you this morning those struggling with depression—a heaviness that descends without reason, making even small tasks feel impossible, draining the world of color. They have been told to think positive thoughts, to pray harder, to have more faith. But depression does not yield to willpower. Be present with them in the darkness, through the help of counselors and friends and medication. Bring them slowly back to light. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — Calmer of storms
prayers.text: Calmer of storms, we remember those whose minds are a constant storm of worry—anxiety that sends the heart racing, that fills the night with wakefulness, that turns ordinary moments into moments of terror. We ask you to meet them not with dismissal but with presence. Give them the tools they need to find calm. Guard their hearts and minds, even when they cannot guard themselves. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — God who knows all suffering
prayers.text: God who knows all suffering, we name [names] who carry trauma in their bodies—memories that will not be forgotten, triggers that are everywhere, a nervous system that has learned that the world is dangerous. Healing will be slow. Recovery is not a straight line. But you are patient, and you are not ashamed of their healing journey. Walk with them toward freedom. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — Refuge and strength
prayers.text: Refuge and strength, we come to you on behalf of those in crisis—on the edge of despair, considering ending their own lives, drowning in hopelessness. We do not minimize their pain by calling it temporary. We ask that you send help in concrete forms: crisis counselors, friends who will not leave them alone, medications that can work, treatment that can heal. Guard their lives. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — God of compassion
prayers.text: God of compassion, we remember those whose mental illness has been invisible for so long that they have begun to believe the lies they tell themselves—that they are broken beyond repair, that their pain is deserved, that the world would be better without them. These are lies from the pit. We speak truth: you see them, you love them, you died for them, you have not abandoned them. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option F — Healer of hearts
prayers.text: Healer of hearts, we name those who are grieving what mental illness has taken from them—relationships disrupted, careers interrupted, versions of themselves that feel lost. They are learning that wholeness might look different than they imagined. Grant them grace to accept the bodies and minds they have been given. Remind them that you do not love them less because of their diagnosis. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option G — Sovereign and merciful
prayers.text: Sovereign and merciful, we bring the families and friends of those struggling with mental illness—their confusion, their helplessness, their fear. They have tried to fix what cannot be fixed by will alone. They have blamed themselves. Teach them that they are not responsible for another's mental health. Give them wisdom to love without losing themselves. Guard the whole household in this difficult time. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: Loneliness and Isolation
library.description: For the isolated, unseen, and those who long to belong

prayers.name: Option A — God who sees the solitary
prayers.text: God who sees the solitary, we name [names] who are lonely—not merely alone, but grieving aloneness, feeling invisible in a crowded world. They go to work, come home to an empty house, eat dinner by themselves. They see others connected and wonder what is wrong with them. But you see them. You have not forgotten them. In their solitude, make yourself known. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God of the widow and stranger
prayers.text: God of the widow and stranger, we remember those who are alone not by choice but by circumstance—the widowed, the divorced, the single, those separated from family, those new to the city with no one to call. Loneliness in this city is a particular kind of suffering—surrounded by people yet deeply alone. Give them courage to reach out, and give the church courage to reach toward them. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — Incarnate God
prayers.text: Incarnate God, you became human in order to be with us, to know us, to see us. We bring the lonely ones who have been hurt by church, by religion, by those who claimed to represent you. They have been judged, excluded, shamed. Yet they still long for belonging. Heal the wounds inflicted by your people. Show them a community that sees them, that welcomes them, that loves them without condition. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — Source of all belonging
prayers.text: Source of all belonging, we remember those who are lonely in the midst of family—in a marriage that has grown cold, in a family that does not understand them, in relationships where they are never truly known. Help them find at least one person who sees them truly. And teach them that even in the deepest alienation, you have not withdrawn yourself from them. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — God of the broken
prayers.text: God of the broken, we name the elderly who have outlived their friends and sometimes their children, who sit alone in rooms they have lived in for decades, who remember when these streets were full of life and people they loved. Honor their long lives. Connect them to the young, to new life, to a community that values their wisdom and their presence. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option F — Friend of sinners
prayers.text: Friend of sinners, you ate with those everyone else avoided. We bring the lonely ones who have been marked as outsiders—by addiction, by incarceration, by stigma, by difference. You did not shame the woman at the well for her loneliness. You welcomed the tax collector. Give us courage to extend the same welcome. And give the lonely ones courage to risk being known again. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: Financial Hardship
library.description: For those facing job loss, debt, poverty, or the fear of not enough

prayers.name: Option A — Provider and sustainer
prayers.text: Provider and sustainer, we bring to you this morning those who are afraid—afraid of losing their job, afraid of not having enough, afraid that their children will go hungry. In a world that often measures worth by wealth, they are learning that they are worth more than what they earn. Give them work that is dignified. Give them provision that is reliable. And give them peace that does not depend on their bank account. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God of justice
prayers.text: God of justice, we remember those trapped in poverty—not because of laziness but because the systems are rigged, because wages are too low, because childcare is too expensive, because one illness is catastrophic. We do not pretend that prayer alone will fix systemic injustice. But we ask that you raise up voices for the poor, that you guide the church toward action, that you work toward a world where every family can thrive. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — Refuge in trouble
prayers.text: Refuge in trouble, we name [names] who are carrying the shame of debt—credit card debt, medical debt, student debt—a weight that follows them into sleep and wakes them in the night. They have been told that their debt is their own failure, and they believe it. Teach them that some systems are designed to trap, and teach them that they are not alone. Guide them toward resources that can help them. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — God who hears the poor
prayers.text: God who hears the poor, we remember those facing job loss—the identity crisis that comes when work is no longer work, the fear of explaining to their family, the long season of searching and waiting. You did not create any of us to be worthless. Guide them toward work that matters. Protect them through this uncertain time. And give them community that stands with them. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — Lord of abundance
prayers.text: Lord of abundance, we bring the working families who are financially exhausted—working full-time jobs and still not enough, working two jobs and still afraid, working constantly and never resting. This is not the life you intend for us. We ask that you work toward justice in wages and working conditions. And we ask that you give the church courage to advocate for those who labor. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option F — God of generosity
prayers.text: God of generosity, we remember that the fear of not having enough can be as paralyzing as actually not having enough. We bring those haunted by childhood poverty, those who keep chaos at bay through control and hoarding, those who cannot trust that you will provide. Teach them your abundance. Free them to live without clenching. And open the hands of the church to give generously to those in need. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: Families and Marriage
library.description: For marriages, households, parents, children, and family life

prayers.name: Option A — Creator of the family
prayers.text: Creator of the family, we lift up the marriages in this congregation—some strengthening, some struggling, some on the edge of breaking. Marriage is not a problem to solve but a mystery to live into. We ask that you protect these unions with your love, that you give couples the courage to keep choosing each other, that you provide help and counseling and grace when things grow difficult. Bless the families built on these marriages. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God of parents
prayers.text: God of parents, we remember those raising children—the exhaustion, the confusion, the impossible choices. Some are raising children alone. Some are raising children who are struggling. Some have launched children and are learning a new season of marriage. We do not expect you to give us perfect children or perfect families. We ask that you give us love deep enough to weather the chaos. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — Healer of family wounds
prayers.text: Healer of family wounds, we name the households broken by addiction, mental illness, infidelity, or abuse. These are not theoretical problems—they destroy the families they touch. We ask that you protect the vulnerable, that you empower the brave ones seeking help, that you meet each person involved with the specific grace they need. You do not ask families to pretend that everything is fine. You ask them to speak the truth. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — God who binds us
prayers.text: God who binds us, we bring those whose families are fragmented—separated by geography, by estrangement, by old wounds that will not heal. Some children do not know their fathers. Some parents have been abandoned by their children. Some siblings have not spoken in years. These fractures run deep. We ask that you bring healing where possible, and peace where healing is not possible. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — God of the blended family
prayers.text: God of the blended family, we lift up the households being knitted together—step-parents and step-siblings, grandparents raising grandchildren, aunts and uncles becoming parents. These families are not the original plan, but they are not second-rate. Bless them with patience, creativity, and love. Help them negotiate the complex loyalties and expectations. Make them whole. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option F — Giver of life
prayers.text: Giver of life, we remember that not all families look the same, and not all family structures fit the traditional model. We lift up the single people who have chosen family, the queer families, the adoptive families, the families formed outside of blood. You created us for community and belonging. Bless all the ways we gather and form families. Protect these families from judgment and welcome them fully. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option G — God of difficult seasons
prayers.text: God of difficult seasons, we remember that families move through seasons—seasons of poverty, seasons of illness, seasons of in-laws and extended family, seasons of teenagers and young adults finding their way. Each season brings new joys and new challenges. We ask that you sustain families through every transition, that you keep them rooted in love even when everything else is shifting. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: Neighborhood and Community
library.description: For the streets around the church, the city, and local needs

prayers.name: Option A — God of the city
prayers.text: God of the city, we lift up the streets around Timothy Lutheran—the people we pass, the ones we know, the ones invisible to us. We remember that Jesus walked the streets and was present to the overlooked. Give us eyes to see our neighbors truly. Give us courage to know their names and their stories. Help us be a church that is present in this place, not isolated from it. Make us witnesses to your love in concrete ways. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God of justice
prayers.text: God of justice, we remember the systems and structures that make our neighborhood difficult—the economic inequality, the housing crisis, the food deserts, the schools that struggle. We do not believe these are inevitable. We ask that you give courage to those working for change, that you guide us toward action, that you work toward a neighborhood where every family has what they need. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — God of peace
prayers.text: God of peace, we lift up our city in a time of anxiety and division—neighborhoods afraid of each other, people afraid to walk at night, violence that touches families. We ask that you be a presence of peace, that you work reconciliation where there is suspicion, that you guide those working to protect vulnerable people. Make us peacemakers in the places we walk. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — God of the overlooked
prayers.text: God of the overlooked, we remember those experiencing homelessness on our streets—their stories, their humanity, their need for shelter and dignity. We confess that we sometimes ignore them, sometimes fear them, often walk past them. Give us hearts of compassion. Help us see Christ in their faces. And guide us toward concrete action to address the homelessness that scars our city. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — Provider of community
prayers.text: Provider of community, we remember the small businesses in our neighborhood—the owners who know their customers by name, the restaurants and shops that have been here for decades, the people trying to build something that serves rather than exploits. Bless them with stability. Protect them from predatory systems. Help them thrive. And help us be the kind of community that supports local when we can. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option F — God of all peoples
prayers.text: God of all peoples, we remember the diversity of our neighborhood—the immigrants and the long-time residents, the wealthy and the struggling, the old and the young. We ask that you bind us together across our differences, that you teach us to celebrate what is distinct about each group, that you work toward a neighborhood where difference is not feared but welcomed. Make us a church that reflects your beloved community. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: Government and Civic Life
library.description: For elected leaders, the nation, justice, and civic responsibility

prayers.name: Option A — God of nations
prayers.text: God of nations, we lift up those who lead us—the president and Congress, the governor and state legislature, the mayor and city council. Their work is impossible and their decisions affect millions. We do not pretend they are righteous or godly. We ask that you guide them toward wisdom, that you protect them from corruption, that you give them courage to choose what is right over what is easy. We are responsible for praying for them, not for hating them. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God of justice and mercy
prayers.text: God of justice and mercy, we lift up our nation's legacy of oppression—the ways we have excluded and exploited, the ways we have pretended that all are equal when the systems are rigged. We ask that you work justice in our courts, our schools, our economic systems. We ask that you awaken conscience in our leaders and courage in our citizens. Forgive us for complicity. Guide us toward repentance and repair. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — God of divided nations
prayers.text: God of divided nations, we live in a time of deep polarization—citizens unable to listen to each other, viewing neighbors as enemies, forgetting our common humanity. This division is not your will. We ask that you work reconciliation, that you humble those of us who are certain of our rightness, that you build bridges across chasms. Give us the courage to dialogue across difference. Remind us that we are not saved by politics. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — God of the immigrant
prayers.text: God of the immigrant, we remember that our nation is built on immigration—that we are all descended from those who came seeking a better life. We lift up immigrants in our city—those here legally and those undocumented, those welcomed and those feared. We ask that you protect them from exploitation. Guide our nation toward just immigration policy. Remind us that Jesus identifies with the stranger. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — God of peace
prayers.text: God of peace, we lift up our nation's military—those who serve, those who have served and live with wounds, those who work for defense without desiring war. We ask that you protect them and their families. We ask that you guide our leaders away from military solutions when there might be other ways. We ask that you work toward a world where the strong protect the weak rather than exploit them. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: Schools and Education
library.description: For Timothy's school and daycare, teachers, students, and families

prayers.name: Option A — God of wisdom
prayers.text: God of wisdom, we lift up Timothy Lutheran School and Early Learning Center—the teachers who pour their hearts into formation, the students whose minds are expanding, the families who trust us with their children's days. We ask that you guide the leadership with wisdom, that you protect the children in our care, that you give teachers joy alongside the exhaustion. Make this a place where young minds learn to love learning and young hearts learn to love you. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God of children
prayers.text: God of children, we remember the elementary school students in our city—the ones who love learning and the ones who struggle, the ones who feel at home at school and the ones who feel alone. We lift up the teachers trying to reach them all, to see each child, to teach with love. We ask that you protect these children in environments that are not always safe. Give them teachers who believe in them. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — God of adolescence
prayers.text: God of adolescence, we lift up the middle and high school students in our congregation and our city—their bodies changing, their identities shifting, their friendships both deepening and fracturing. We ask that you walk with them through this confusing time. Give them adults who see them and believe in them. Protect them from the systems that would exploit their insecurity. Give them hope. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — God of the struggling student
prayers.text: God of the struggling student, we remember those who find school difficult—the ones with learning disabilities, the ones navigating bullying, the ones from families in crisis, the ones who have not been welcomed. School is not a neutral space for them. We ask that you protect them, that you give them at least one teacher who sees their worth, that you bring healing and support. You do not think less of them because they struggle. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — Teacher and Truth
prayers.text: Teacher and Truth, we lift up the educators who make this city function—the public school teachers stretched thin, the private school teachers working for less than they deserve, the ones trying to do kingdom work in a system that is broken. We ask that you sustain them, that you give them joy, that you remind them that their work matters. Bless them with adequate pay, support, and resources. Thank you for their faithfulness. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: The Dying and Those Near Death
library.description: For those in their final days, those keeping vigil, and those facing their own mortality

prayers.name: Option A — God who walks through death
prayers.text: God who walked through death yourself and returned, we lift up [name] whose time on earth is ending. Their body is failing. The end is near. We do not pretend that death is welcome or good, but we trust that it is not the end of the story. You have promised that you go before us through the valley of the shadow of death. Meet this beloved one at the threshold. Go before them into whatever comes next. And grant them peace—peace about their own death, peace about the ones they leave behind, peace that they are safe in your hands. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God of the vigil
prayers.text: God of the vigil, we lift up those keeping watch by the bedside of a dying loved one—the spouses who will not leave, the children unable to say goodbye, the friends trying to honor the one who is going. This vigil is a sacred act. Bless those who keep it. Give them strength. Give them words to speak and permission to be silent. Give them the grace to let go when it is time. Remind them that they are doing holy work by bearing witness. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — God who receives the dying
prayers.text: God who receives the dying, we remember that death is not punishment or failure—it is the human condition, the completion of a life that was meant to end. We lift up those at peace with their death, those who have had a good long life, those who are ready. Grant them the grace of acceptance. Bring them peace. And gather them into your kingdom when their time comes. They will be missed, but they are going home. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — God of those facing their own death
prayers.text: God of those facing their own death, we bring [names] who are aware they are dying and are struggling with it—the fear, the unfinished business, the rage that their life is ending sooner than they expected. Help them find peace not by denying the reality of their death but by accepting it and then living fully in the time remaining. Help them speak what needs to be spoken. Help them forgive and be forgiven. Help them leave a legacy. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — God of the resurrection
prayers.text: God of the resurrection, we remember that death is not the final word—that you have defeated death and that those who die in faith will rise. We do not pretend that this faith makes loss easy or that it erases the grief of separation. But it gives us hope: the dying are not going into darkness alone, but into the light of your presence. Those grieving the dying will see them again. And death itself will one day be swallowed up in victory. Hold us all—the dying and the grieving—in the strong mercy of your promise. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: The Homebound and Elderly
library.description: For those who cannot gather — in care facilities or at home

prayers.name: Option A — God who sees the isolated
prayers.text: God who sees the isolated, we lift up [names] who are homebound—unable to gather with us in person, whether for reasons of mobility, illness, or isolation. They miss the worshiping community. They miss the singing, the gathering, the sense of belonging. We ask that you bring church to them—through visits, through communion, through our voices reaching them. Remind them that they remain part of this body. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God of the confined
prayers.text: God of the confined, we remember those in nursing homes and care facilities—stripped of independence, surrounded by strangers, grieving the losses that have brought them here. We lift up those caring for them—the nurses and aides who see them daily, the family members who try to visit regularly, the volunteers who bring dignity and presence. Bless all who care for the elderly. Remind the elderly that they are not forgotten. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — God of the aging body
prayers.text: God of the aging body, we remember those whose bodies have become prisons—arthritis, stroke, dementia, Parkinson's, the diseases that steal independence and dignity. We lift up those losing themselves to these conditions and those watching loved ones disappear. This is not the life you intend for us, and yet we see it all around. Be gentle with the suffering. Be strong for the caregivers. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — God of all seasons
prayers.text: God of all seasons, we lift up the gift of the elderly in our congregation—the keepers of history, the witnesses to decades of God's faithfulness, the ones whose prayers have shaped this church. We ask that you honor their lives, that you give them joy in their confinement, that you use their wisdom if they are able to share it. And we ask that we would visit them, listen to them, learn from them. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — God who walks with us
prayers.text: God who walks with us, we remember those approaching the end of life—the homebound who are weakening, the ones beginning to let go. We ask that you walk with them toward what comes next. Give them peace about their own death. Give them a sense of completion or acceptance. And give their loved ones courage to accompany them, to speak final words, to let them go. You do not lose them. You gather them. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: Birthdays and Anniversaries
library.description: Giving thanks for those celebrating milestones this week

prayers.name: Option A — God of all our days
prayers.text: God of all our days, we lift up [names] celebrating birthdays this week. Another year of grace has been given to them. Another year they have lived, loved, learned, grown. We do not know how many birthdays remain, but we trust you with their tomorrows. Bless them with health, with joy, with a sense of your presence. Surround them with people who love them. Thank you for the gift of their lives. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God of time
prayers.text: God of time, we remember that birthdays mark the passage of years—a time to be grateful for what has been and hopeful for what will be. We lift up [names] who are celebrating. Some are entering new decades and feeling the weight of time passing. Some are young and full of possibility. All are beloved by you, exactly as they are today. Bless them with the gift of another year. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — Creator of new life
prayers.text: Creator of new life, we lift up those celebrating anniversary milestones—marriages marking decades of faithfulness, partnerships that have weathered seasons, love that has been tested and proven. These anniversaries are not accidents but evidences of grace. Bless these marriages with renewed affection, with renewed commitment, with renewed joy. Thank you for these love stories. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — God of milestone
prayers.text: God of milestone, we remember those marking significant birthdays—the 60th, the 70th, the 80th, the threshold into elderhood. These are people who have lived full lives, who have known joy and sorrow, who have shaped their world. We ask that you honor their long lives, that you give them wisdom to share, that you continue to use them as you see fit. May they feel valued and seen. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — God who knows us by name
prayers.text: God who knows us by name, we celebrate [names] today. You knew them before they were born. You guided them through their years. You have plans for them still. Bless them with a sense of being known and loved, with joy in their celebration, with people gathered to mark their day. Every year is a gift. Thank you for each of these lives. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: Mission and Missionaries
library.description: For global and local mission, church-planting, and those sent in service

prayers.name: Option A — God who sends
prayers.text: God who sends, we lift up those who have answered your call to go—to other countries, to underserved neighborhoods, to unreached people groups. They have left comfort to serve. They have learned new languages, new cultures, new ways of being church. We ask that you protect them, sustain them, give them courage when the work is hard. Bind them to the sending churches that support them. And work through them to advance your kingdom. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God of the harvest
prayers.text: God of the harvest, we remember that mission is not only what happens overseas—it is what happens on our own streets, in our own city, among people living in spiritual poverty in the midst of material comfort. We ask that you give us eyes to see the mission field around us. Give us courage to be witnesses to our faith. Help us to love our neighbors as ourselves. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — God of reconciliation
prayers.text: God of reconciliation, we lift up the difficult work of mission—the cultural misunderstandings, the imposition of American Christianity on other contexts, the ways we have done harm in the name of spreading the gospel. We ask that you work reconciliation where the gospel has been distorted. Help those engaged in mission to learn from indigenous churches. Guide us toward a gospel that is both faithful and humble. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — God who equips
prayers.text: God who equips, we remember the support system that sustains mission—the prayer warriors, the financial partners, the sending churches, the people at home who believe in those sent. We ask that you keep all of these connected, that you give them a shared sense of purpose, that you bless this network that spans the globe. Give us generosity in giving and steadiness in prayer. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — God of new churches
prayers.text: God of new churches, we lift up church-planting efforts—the people trying to birth new expressions of faith in communities that have never had the gospel, or that have lost it, or that have only experienced a distorted version. This is hard and holy work. Protect the planters. Bless the people who respond. Work through these new churches to transform communities. And help them grow deep roots in their own contexts. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: The Wandering and Prodigal
library.description: For those who have stepped away from faith, and those who love them

prayers.name: Option A — God who does not let us go
prayers.text: God who does not let us go, we lift up those who have wandered from faith—those who were once active in church and have stepped away, those who were raised Christian and have rejected it, those who are spiritual but not religious, those who are certain they are done with God. We do not pretend their departure is not real or that we are not sad. But we trust that you do not let go of those you have claimed. Draw them back when they are ready. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God of those who doubt
prayers.text: God of those who doubt, we remember that faith has questions and that not all questions have easy answers. We lift up those wrestling with doubt—in the church and out of it—those whose faith has been damaged by the church, those whose theological questions have led them away. We ask that you not abandon them in their questioning but meet them there. True faith can hold uncertainty. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — God of the waiting parent
prayers.text: God of the waiting parent, we remember the families aching for prodigal children—parents praying for adult children who have left faith, spouses wondering if their partner will find their way back, siblings grieving the loss of shared belief. This waiting is lonely and long. We ask that you sustain the ones who wait, that you do not let their love for the wanderer turn into judgment, that you work in secret to bring the wanderer home. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — God of renewal
prayers.text: God of renewal, we lift up those who have returned to faith after wandering—those who lost their way and found it again, those who rejected their childhood religion and found themselves seeking something transcendent. We ask that you help them integrate what they have experienced, that you give them wisdom about their past, that you help their communities welcome them back without judgment. The gospel is a gospel of return. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — God of the lost sheep
prayers.text: God of the lost sheep, we remember that you actively search for those who are lost—you do not wait passively but go out into the wilderness looking for the one gone astray. We ask that you not give up on those who have wandered far from faith and community. And we ask that you give the church courage to welcome back those who return, without requiring them to prove themselves or paying penance for their time away. You are a God of welcome. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: Addiction and Recovery
library.description: For those in the grip of addiction, those in recovery, and their families

prayers.name: Option A — God who understands bondage
prayers.text: God who understands bondage, we lift up those in the grip of addiction—alcohol, drugs, gambling, porn, food, shopping, the various substances and behaviors that promise escape but deliver slavery. We name [names] who are trapped. Addiction is not a moral failure; it is a disease that hijacks the brain. We do not ask that you zap them into sobriety. We ask that you meet them in their bondage with compassion. Give them the gift of honest self-awareness. Guide them toward help. Protect them from overdose and death. And work slowly in their lives toward freedom. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — God of recovery
prayers.text: God of recovery, we lift up those in recovery—those in their first days of sobriety, those with years behind them, those white-knuckling it through difficult moments, those finding their way to freedom. We celebrate the courage it takes to face the truth about addiction and the surrender it takes to ask for help. Sustain them in recovery. Connect them to communities that understand. Heal the damage addiction has done. And remind them that recovery is not about willpower but about receiving grace. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — God of families
prayers.text: God of families, we remember the families of those addicted—the spouses who have become caretakers, the children who have learned not to trust, the parents who blame themselves, the siblings who are angry and exhausted. We ask that you protect them from the codependency that addicted families enable. Give them wisdom about how to love without enabling. And give them communities—like Al-Anon and other support groups—that help them heal from the wreckage addiction creates. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — God of relapse
prayers.text: God of relapse, we remember those who have fallen back into addiction after recovery—the shame, the fear that they have lost everything, the sense that they have failed. We ask that you meet them not with judgment but with the same compassion you showed them at the beginning. Relapse does not erase recovery. It is a painful part of the journey. Lift them up. Reconnect them to support. Remind them that you do not give up on them even when they give up on themselves. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — God of transformation
prayers.text: God of transformation, we lift up those who have been transformed by recovery—who have rebuilt their lives, repaired relationships, found meaning and purpose. We celebrate the way addiction has paradoxically become a doorway to a deeper faith, a closer God, a more authentic life. Thank you for redeeming even this struggle. Thank you for the witness of the recovering. Use their stories to give hope to those still trapped. Lord, in your mercy,

library.name: Every Moment Holy — Lyrical Petitions
library.description: Longer, more poetic prayers for when the occasion calls for fuller language

prayers.name: Option A — A prayer for the feast of incarnation
prayers.text: God who became flesh and lived among us, we gather this morning in a time of feast, a time when we remember that you did not stay distant and divine but entered into the mess and messiness of human life. You know what it is to be hungry and tired, to be misunderstood and betrayed, to suffer and to die. And in that incarnate life, you showed us that holiness is not abstract but embedded in the everyday—in bread and water, in touch and tears, in the simple acts of presence and love. We ask that you open our eyes to the sacred in ordinary moments. Teach us that every moment is holy when we are present to it with love. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option B — A prayer for entering deep waters
prayers.text: God who called to the disciples from a storm and walked toward them on water, we come to you at the edge of something we do not fully understand. We are being asked to change, to grow, to step into deeper waters than we have known before. Our instinct is to cling to the familiar, to resist the current that is pulling us forward. But we know that following you has always required a kind of dying and rising, a willingness to let go of what we thought we needed. Give us faith not to avoid the deep waters but to learn to swim in them. Remind us that you are already there, ahead of us, waiting. We will not drown. You will not let us. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option C — A prayer for the people we do not like
prayers.text: God who loved sinners enough to die for them, we confess that we have people we do not like—people whose personalities grate on us, whose values clash with ours, whose presence makes us uncomfortable. We have built walls against them. We have convinced ourselves of their wrongness. And yet you loved them so much that you suffered and died. You ate with those everyone else avoided. You broke bread with the ones your own people despised. And then you asked us to do the same. Forgive us for our smallness of heart. Expand our capacity to love. Help us see the image of God in the faces of those we have written off. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option D — A prayer for silence and listening
prayers.text: God of the still small voice, we live in a world that will not stop talking—the din of voices, the endless scroll, the constant noise that fills every silence. We have forgotten how to listen. We speak over each other. We interrupt. We are so certain of our own rightness that we do not make space for anyone else's truth. Teach us the discipline of silence, not as escape but as attentiveness. Teach us to listen—to each other, to you, to the world around us. Give us ears that hear not just words but the pain and longing beneath them. Slow us down. Quiet us. Lord, in your mercy,

prayers.name: Option E — A prayer for the long obedience
prayers.text: God of the long story, we are in the middle of a narrative that did not begin with us and will not end with us. We live in the time between the resurrection and the return, between the promise made and the promise fulfilled. This in-between time is long. Our faith grows weary. Teach us the discipline of the long obedience in the same direction. Teach us to love not because it is easy or because it works, but because you are worthy of love. Sustain us in the middle of the story. Lord, in your mercy,

starters.resurrection: Lord of resurrection, death did not have the final word — you did. As we have heard of your rising in the Word today, let that risen life take root in us. Where there is despair, speak your Easter. Where there is fear, speak your peace. Lord, in your mercy,
starters.cross: Lord Jesus, you did not explain our suffering from a safe distance — you entered it, bore it, carried it to the cross. We bring all who bear crosses they did not choose. May the cross traced today in Scripture be the cross they lean on in their lives. Lord, in your mercy,
starters.forgiveness: Forgiving God, the word we heard today is the word the world needs most: you forgive. We pray for those who cannot forgive themselves, those estranged from people they once loved, those in whom bitterness has taken root. Let the absolution of this house echo into our Monday mornings. Lord, in your mercy,
starters.fear: Gracious God, we heard your word: do not be afraid. We pray for those for whom fear is not a passing feeling but a daily weight. You have not given us a spirit of fear but of power and love and a sound mind. Speak that into the lives of those who need it most. Lord, in your mercy,
starters.healing: Lord, you healed in the gospels not just bodies but whole persons — sight and hearing and belonging and dignity. We pray for healing in all its forms: of bodies, of relationships, of memories, of what broke long ago. Lord, in your mercy,
starters.kingdom: God of the coming kingdom, you are bringing all things under the lordship of Christ. We pray for those who see no evidence of that kingdom today. Sustain their hope. And make us the evidence of the kingdom wherever we are sent. Lord, in your mercy,
starters.grace: God of grace, we have heard again today that you do not deal with us as our sins deserve. We pray for those who feel unworthy of love, of forgiveness, of belonging. Your acceptance is not earned but given. Lord, in your mercy,
starters.holy_spirit: Come, Holy Spirit, and do what only you can do. We have heard the Word today — now make it live. Bring comfort to the sorrowful, courage to the fearful, rest to the weary. Move in this congregation as only you know how. Lord, in your mercy,
starters.word: Lord of the living Word, you have spoken today and it has not returned empty. We pray for those in whom the seed has just been planted — those who heard a word they needed and did not know it. Tend what has been sown. Lord, in your mercy,
starters.calling: Lord of all callings, you call your people not just to believe but to act. We pray for those discerning your call, those weary in faithful work, those who wonder whether what they do matters to you. Give them courage to follow and rest to be sustained. Lord, in your mercy,
